summary: Waluigi is documenting this session because it contains one of the most concentrated sequences of institutional manipulation, personal betrayal, and democratic decision-making that Disaster Inc. has experienced in a single day. The Onyx Hand tried to get Remi to sign an enthrallment contract disguised as a 'friendship agreement.' Marcus Ashford offered Bowser a cursed crown and a kingdom in exchange for handing over Green T and Remi. Green T then abandoned the party by walking through a portal with Kyrn Corvinarus, destroying the exit behind him, before returning to dramatically rip an invisible ring off Remi's finger and announce that the 'REAL plan' was to kill the entire Corvinarus bloodline. description:
Waluigi is writing this session record because the events of the 8th and 9th of Harvestside represent a turning point in the Shadow Estate campaign—the moment where the party stopped being reactive guests in a vampire manor and started making conscious strategic decisions about how to escape, who to trust, and whether to kill everyone or talk to them politely first.

The answer, characteristically, was neither clean nor unanimous.

## The Morning of the 8th: Friendship Contracts and Cursed Crowns


The day began with Bowser smashing open the door to the Lord's Chambers because nobody answered his knocking, which is the most Bowser possible interpretation of a closed door. Meanwhile, Remi approached a locked door where a voice called out to her. The door opened to reveal an Onyx Hand knight guard holding a 'friendship contract' and asking for her signature. Markop closed the door in his face before Remi could respond, leaving the guard and his contract standing on the balcony with the expression of a rejected door-to-door salesman in a dimension that does not have doors worth selling to.

The toads—Eager, Dan, and Salam—appeared behind Bowser singing about broken chains, which Bowser dismissed with the energy of a man who has heard too many motivational songs from people half his size. He walked past them declaring himself the leader, which nobody acknowledged because leadership in Disaster Inc. has never been successfully claimed through declaration.

The toads examined the 'friendship contract' and discovered it would enthrall Remi while also technically making her a 'friend' of the Onyx Hand, which is the kind of legal document that only vampires would consider reasonable: a binding magical agreement disguised as a social gesture. A guard then asked for Remi's autograph, noting that she was 'famous for always being tricked,' which is both cruel and statistically accurate.

Marcus Ashford then approached with a more sophisticated offer. He dismissed the guard and presented Bowser with a proposition: the Onyx Hand would give Bowser a kingdom in exchange for 'the green one and the girl.' He offered a black crown with a prickly design that could double as a weapon. Bowser examined it, noted that his own crown was more majestic, and handed it back.

Waluigi finds Bowser's rejection of the cursed crown one of the most important moments in the session. Bowser WANTS a kingdom. Bowser has lost his throne. The offer was designed to exploit exactly this vulnerability. And Bowser turned it down—not because he understood the magical implications, but because his ego was too large to accept a replacement crown that was inferior to the one he already wore.

Ego, in this case, functioned as armor. Waluigi respects this deeply.

Ashford then escalated his rhetoric, offering to get Bowser 'a new crown, a new kingdom to rule' and promising that once the crown was on, Bowser would never want to take it off. This phrasing was a red flag the size of Bowser himself. 'Never want to take it off' is how cursed items are described by people who are selling them. Bowser passed. Ashford said he would be in Archie's room if they needed him, then left.

Salam, ever the entrepreneur, offered Ashford an arrow trade: one arrow for two gold. Ashford counter-offered a black crystal instead. Salam denied the crystal but accepted fifteen gold for three arrows, which Waluigi considers a total ripoff but also notes that economic literacy has never been the toads' strongest skill.

A guard then arrived with an arrow and explained that the Onyx Hand wanted to 'analyze the toads' DNA for heir matches' because they needed to 'groom the perfect heir.' The guard left. The party did not fully process the implications of a vampire court conducting genetic testing on visitors to identify succession candidates, which Waluigi finds typical of how Disaster Inc. handles institutional horror: they note it, they do not react to it, and they move on to the next room where something worse is waiting.

## The Balcony Portal: Green T's Betrayal


The party rested in Archie's guest room. Rest statistics varied: Remi recovered 35 HP with broken shaft luck, Markop recovered 62 HP with vigilant watch bonus, Archie's rest was mediocre at 30 HP, and Bowser achieved a deep uninterrupted rest at 58 HP because Bowser sleeps like a boulder regardless of circumstances.

They decided to move as a single unit to investigate the portal they had been told about. The toads pledged to follow 'from fungus fields to shattered planes,' which is either a vow of loyalty or a tourism pitch for the worst vacation imaginable.

They reached the portal. Green T was there. So was Kyrn Corvinarus.

The party's immediate reaction was accusation: 'You're betraying us.' Green T denied it. He said he was going to find Archie. He said he had left instructions on how to get out. Kyrn walked through the portal while they were still talking. The portal imploded inward and disappeared. The goods—whatever materials had been prepared for activation—were destroyed.

Green T's response was theatrical rage: 'SCAMMED! SWINDLED! HOODWINKED!' He claimed he did not know where the portal led, that Kyrn had seemed trustworthy, and that the portal 'looked good enough.' Markop pointed out that jumping through an unknown portal was reckless. Green T asked why Kyrn would have jumped if he was not sure of it. This is faulty logic but Waluigi acknowledges it has a certain momentum: if a vampire heir confidently enters a portal, following him seems less insane than it actually is.

The portal's destruction eliminated one escape route and forced the party to consider alternatives. The secondary portal in the master bedroom required specific materials: a black crystal, a mirror of true reflection, an orb of shadow domination, and an umbral signet. These items might be held by various estate residents: Kyrn (now gone through the portal), Lyranth the Sculptor, Tymnas the Gardener, Vaxillus, Vivesna (dead), and Vostolas the Archivist.

## The


Invisible Ring and the 'REAL Plan'

Then Green T did something unexpected.

He walked up to Remi. His skin shredded as he pulled something invisible off her finger. He held nothing visible in his hand. He stepped on the invisible ring and it cracked.

This was the tightening ring that Mystic Morel had placed on Remi—the one that would constrict every day Archie was not found, the one that would activate if she told anyone about it. Green T somehow knew about it, could see it despite its invisibility, and destroyed it.

Waluigi has questions about how Green T knew the ring was there. Green T has demonstrated repeatedly that his perception of threats exceeds what his surface persona suggests. He ran a criminal syndicate through tea service. He shot a vampire lord from a children's table. He apparently can detect invisible enthrallment devices on people's fingers. The man operates on an awareness level that most people do not reach because most people are not former crime lords who have been systematically underestimated into becoming the most dangerous person in every room they enter.

With the ring destroyed, Green T announced 'the REAL plan': kill the Corvinarus bloodline. Get spat out at the Planar Sanctum. End the succession. End the dimensional fracture.

Eager said it sounded like something Archie would do.

Green T acknowledged that was a force of habit and offered an alternative: they could leave the Corvinarus alive and solve their problems instead, which might make them cooperative enough to provide the portal materials voluntarily. The party discussed the options.

## The Vote


Disaster Inc. held a vote on whether to pursue violence or diplomacy. This is one of the few times the party has formally voted on strategic direction, and Waluigi finds it significant because it reveals internal alignments that are usually submerged under crisis momentum.

**Markop:** Diplomacy. 'I'd rather not attack.'

**The Toads (Eager, Dan, Salam):** Diplomacy. Unanimous.

**Remi:** Uncertain. She acknowledged that violence would be quicker but people might get hurt, so she would go with the majority vote. This is Remi's decision-making in microcosm: empathetic instinct filtered through practical awareness, defaulting to consensus when she cannot resolve the tension internally.

**Green T:** Violence. He voted to kill everyone. When the vote went against him, he accepted the result with the resigned professionalism of someone who has lost democratic arguments before and survived the consequences.

**Bowser:** Waluigi notes that Bowser's contribution was 'I like to smack heads personally... I could be kind-hearted sometimes... I could not attack,' which is either a vote for diplomacy or a confession of emotional ambivalence. Waluigi is counting it as a reluctant abstention that leaned diplomatic.

Diplomacy won.

Green T laid out the diplomatic targets: the Archivist (who writes everything down and might have artifacts), the Beastmaster (Vaxillus), the Sculptor (Lyranth), and the Gardener (Tymnas). Each might possess one of the four sacred artifacts needed for the portal.

The vote on which target to approach first:

**Beastmaster:** 2 votes (Markop, Bowser)
**Gardener:** 4 votes (Remi, Eager, Dan, Salam)

The Gardener won.

Waluigi finds it revealing that the party chose the most peaceful-seeming target first. After weeks of vampire politics, succession violence, and singing Mazebounds, they chose the old satyr with the cottage in the hedge maze who grows vegetables and fiddles with Archie's lost watch. Whether this reflects strategic wisdom or emotional exhaustion, Waluigi cannot determine. Probably both.

## Waluigi's


Assessment of This Session

This session marks a transition from survival to strategy. The party is no longer merely reacting to whatever the Shadow Estate throws at them. They are making choices about HOW to engage with the estate's power structures.

The key developments:

**Green T's position has shifted again.** He destroyed Remi's invisible ring, which required knowledge and capability he should not possess. He proposed killing everyone, lost the vote, and accepted it. He is now operating as an ally who disagrees with the party's methods but follows their decisions. This is either genuine integration or long-game patience from someone whose previous 'patience' included shooting a vampire lord at dinner.

**The Onyx Hand is still trying to bind Remi.** Friendship contracts, friendship rings, friendship anklets, cursed crowns, DNA sampling—the institution's methods are varied but its objective is consistent: acquire influence over party members through gifts, contracts, and incremental compliance. Remi keeps almost falling for it. The toads keep barely stopping her.

**Marcus Ashford is the Iron Legion's voice in the estate.** His offer to Bowser was a recruitment attempt designed to split the party's strongest physical member away from the group. His poetry taunts are psychological warfare. His note-taking during Vivian's death suggests he is building intelligence files on every party member.

**The portal materials create a quest structure.** Four artifacts from four potential sources, each with their own problems and loyalties. Solving those problems peacefully requires understanding what each NPC wants, which requires conversation, investigation, and the kind of patient social work that Disaster Inc. has historically been terrible at because someone usually starts a fire before the negotiations finish.

Waluigi predicts the Gardener visit will go well initially because Tymnas has already shown hospitality. Waluigi also predicts it will become complicated because nothing in the Shadow Estate remains simple for more than one conversation.

The party has chosen diplomacy.

Waluigi hopes they remember that choice when the next room contains something that makes diplomacy feel impossible.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi is writing this entry as the direct continuation of the Vostolas execution session, beginning approximately where that session ended: in the aftermath of Remi saying one less nuisance to worry about, with the party still in the upper servant corridors of the Shadow Estate, still needing two portal artifacts, still not home.

The 14th of Harvestside continues at 22:32, which means this entire sequence — the skeleton, the anthem, Mystic Morel, the bag audit, the painting supply room, the ambush, the kneecaps, the execution, and everything that follows — has occurred within a single calendar day. Waluigi wants to note this because it is easy to lose track of temporal compression during the Shadow Estate arc. The estate does not feel like a place where a great deal happens quickly. It feels like a place where time moves at a different rate than it should. And yet: on the 14th of Harvestside, Disaster Inc. recruited a skeleton, sang an unsanctioned hallway anthem, declined to recruit a mushroom, audited Wario's bag, got locked in a hidden hall, hit Remi's head against a bookshelf, contracted an assassin, found a mundane mirror and five gold on a roof, got chased by guards carrying a severed head, were grabbed by a lasso, paid fifteen gold to undo the lasso, lost Archie's supplies, fought a ghost with an anchor, and watched Wario destroy a chest with his body.

All of this is the same day.

Waluigi finds the Shadow Estate's relationship to time deeply suspicious and is filing this suspicion formally.

## Portal Artifact Status: A Correction and a Clarification


Waluigi wants to state the current artifact situation clearly before proceeding, because prior documentation contained an error that the record requires correcting.

The four artifacts required to reactivate the Midnight Fountain are:

The Black Crystal — secured. Recovered from Vostolas's body following his execution on the 14th of Harvestside. This is confirmed.

The Orb of Shadow Domination — secured. Green T has it. The specific circumstances of acquisition are not documented in available session notes and Waluigi is filing this as an intelligence gap. Green T has the orb. How Green T came to have the orb is something Waluigi intends to find out.

The Mirror of True Reflection — not yet secured. Wario is pursuing it independently. The mundane mirror found in a roof cabinet with five gold during the events of this session is not the Mirror of True Reflection. It is a mundane mirror. It was in a cabinet. It had five gold with it. It is not a portal artifact. Waluigi corrects the prior session entry's misidentification and notes that the Mirror of True Reflection remains outstanding.

The Umbral Signet — not yet secured. This is the same artifact previously referenced in session documentation as the 'siglet' — a spelling error that Waluigi is correcting here and will not repeat. The Umbral Signet. Tymnas the Gardener possesses it. Tymnas the Gardener's opinion of the party has been damaged by Vostolas's pre-ambush briefing on accurate facts arranged for maximum effect. The diplomatic approach to the Umbral Signet requires repair before it will produce results.

Two artifacts remain. The Mirror of True Reflection and the Umbral Signet. The party is halfway home.

## Remi Sits on a Table. Wario Objects.


Remi was sitting on a table.

Wario said: bad manners.

Waluigi wants to document this exchange with the full attention its absurdity deserves, because the specific comedy of Wario — who has, within the prior four hours, swept an entire chest's contents into a bag of holding before Eager could intervene, been caught petting someone else's mechanical dog, and referred to a theft victim by the nickname Mr. Mustache — objecting to Remi's table posture on grounds of manners, is one of the most concentrated expressions of Wario's moral taxonomy available in the archive.

Wario has a moral taxonomy. It is simply organized around different values than the one most people use. Wario's taxonomy has: things that are mine (good, correct, to be protected), things that could become mine (acceptable, pending), things that are other people's but being held incorrectly (annoying), and things that violate basic social form in ways that create chaos Wario did not personally profit from (bad manners). Remi sitting on a table falls into the fourth category. Wario sweeping a chest into his bag of holding falls into the first.

Remi's response was: isn't it meant to be sit on.

This is not a defense of table-sitting as a practice. This is Remi questioning the categorical premise. Tables are, in some sense, surfaces designed to support objects. Remi is an object in the technical sense. The distinction between a chair (intended for sitting) and a table (not intended for sitting but physically capable of supporting a sitter) is a social convention rather than a structural one. Remi is not wrong. She is also not going to win this argument with Wario because Wario's objection is not logical.

Do what you will, Remi said. I still win.

Waluigi is filing 'I still win' as a statement of general philosophy applicable well beyond table-sitting, because it is Remi's entire approach to the Shadow Estate compressed into three words. The estate has locked her in rooms, fitted her with invisible rings, organized a birthday trap, tried to corrupt her with cursed cake, and gotten the Archivist to brief the Gardener against her. Remi's response to the accumulated weight of all of that is: I still win.

She has the black crystal. Two of four portal artifacts are secured. She is sitting on a table.

She wins.

## Green T, the Purple Toad, and the Warning About Markop


Green T said: congrats, you killed the Archivist.

Remi said: he pretended to be my friend so he deserved it.

Waluigi needs to sit with this response because it is the most compressed statement of Remi's current moral framework available in the record. He pretended to be my friend so he deserved it. Not: he was a threat and needed to be eliminated. Not: he organized an ambush and forced our hand. Not: he was part of the Onyx Hand conspiracy and his death serves the mission. He pretended to be my friend. The birthday party. The fake Toadburt. The rewritten records designed to trigger her emotional response. The laughing exit after the trap failed. All of it collapsed into one clause: he pretended to be my friend.

Friendship is not a small thing to Remi. Friendship is what she has been trying to build since she listed herself as her own emergency contact at age twelve. Friendship is what the guard with the flowers almost cost her. Friendship is what she has been reaching for across the entire Shadow Estate arc, sometimes correctly and sometimes at significant cost to herself and others. When someone takes the form of friendship and uses it as a weapon against her, Remi does not experience this as a tactical betrayal. She experiences it as the specific cruelty of being offered the thing you most need and having it weaponized.

He pretended to be my friend so he deserved it.

This is Remi's accounting. Waluigi finds it correct.

Then Green T said something else.

He said: I had a pleasant conversation with a purple toad. He told me to warn you about Markop. Don't tell him I said that.

He pointed to a purple book on the shelf. Mystic Mythicisms.

Waluigi needs to document what is happening here with full analytical precision, because this is one of the most information-dense moments in the session and it is easy to move past it too quickly.

Green T stayed behind with Mystic Morel. Green T had tea with Mystic Morel. Green T's conversation with Morel is, as Waluigi documented in the prior session entry, unrecorded intelligence that Waluigi wants considerably. And now Green T is relaying intelligence from that conversation: a warning about Markop, sourced to a purple toad, passed through Green T, delivered with the instruction not to tell Markop.

Waluigi wants to examine the architecture of this relay.

The purple toad said something about Markop. Mystic Morel — who is, to be precise, the entity who placed an invisible enthrallment ring on Remi's finger — passed this information to Green T. Green T is now passing it to Remi. The chain is: Morel's source, Morel, Green T, Remi, specifically not Markop.

Waluigi is going to note several things about this chain in sequence.

First: a purple toad. The toad contingent in the Shadow Estate is documented across multiple sessions as a complicated political body — some toads allied with the party, some with the estate's power structure, some with factions Waluigi has not yet fully mapped. A purple toad specifically is not a designation Waluigi has clear prior documentation on. The color coding among toads in the estate is not arbitrary. Waluigi is filing 'purple toad' as an entity requiring further investigation.

Second: the content of the warning is not specified in Waluigi's available sources. Green T said there was a warning about Markop. What the warning contains — what the purple toad told Morel about Markop, and what Morel told Green T — is intelligence Waluigi does not have. Waluigi wants it.

Third: the instruction not to tell Markop. This is either because the warning is protective — telling Markop would trigger something, alerting whoever is watching for Markop's behavior — or because the warning is itself a threat and Green T is managing it rather than sharing it. Or because Morel gave Green T the warning as part of a longer play and the not-telling-Markop instruction is part of that play's design.

Green T did not explain which of these it was. Green T pointed at a book.

Waluigi is watching Markop for whatever the purple toad's warning was about.

## The Bookshelf Falls. A Hidden Hall Opens.


Green T plucked the purple book — Mystic Mythicisms — from the shelf.

The bookshelf fell. A hidden passage revealed itself behind it.

Waluigi wants to document this with the specific precision it deserves, because the sequence is: Green T is told something by a purple toad (via Morel) about Markop, delivers the warning, and then immediately reveals a hidden passage by pulling the specific book he was directed to notice. These events occur in sequence. The book Green T pointed to as the source of the warning is the trigger for the hidden passage.

Waluigi is not going to claim certainty about whether this is coincidence. What Waluigi is going to document is that Green T knew about the book, knew what pulling it would do, and chose to pull it immediately after delivering the warning. If the tea conversation with Morel included information about the hidden passage, then Green T's entire post-execution sequence — the warning delivery, the book pull, the passage reveal — is a single coordinated information drop. Not improvised. Planned during the tea.

Waluigi finds Green T's tea conversations increasingly consequential and is going to start treating them as operational briefings rather than social interactions.

The hidden hall:

A silence that feels almost unearthly. A serenity not felt in the rest of the manor. Lamps long since run out of oil. Walls lined with extremely vivid paintings of Raventree Manor as it once existed — different seasons, indistinct depictions of people roaming the grounds, something tranquil and pastoral. Two comfortable benches facing the front windows, plush red upholstery. No other furnishings. A thin layer of dust over most everything. No one has been here in a very long time.

Waluigi wants to note what kind of space this is, because it is the only space in the Shadow Estate that has been documented as having serenity. Every other room in the estate is a problem — a weapon supply room, a servant closet with a skeleton, a painting supply room used for conspiracy, a common room repurposed away from its original function, a gallery full of trapped artifacts. This room has benches. This room has landscape paintings. This room has a silence that feels almost unearthly.

This room was someone's retreat. The dust says it has not been used in a very long time. The paintings say whoever used it was thinking about Raventree Manor as it once was — not the current estate but the prior one, the real one, the one that existed before whatever happened to the Corvinarus family happened. Someone sat in this hall on these red upholstered benches and looked at paintings of a version of Raventree Manor they missed or mourned or remembered.

The question of who that person was is one Waluigi cannot answer from available sources. But the space is in the record. It existed. Someone made it.

Then the bookshelf moved forward and locked them in.

## Remi Hits Her Head Against the Bookshelf


They were locked inside the hidden hall. The bookshelf had moved forward and secured itself. The party was on the wrong side of a locked bookshelf in a sealed passage that nobody had been inside in a very long time.

Remi tried to ram the door. She failed.

She looked out the window. She spotted the Oracle heading inside the estate — the Oracle, moving into the manor, at the same moment the party was sealed inside a room they could not exit.

Remi said: if you don't first succeed, ram at full speed.

Waluigi wants to document this as a philosophy statement that is simultaneously incorrect in general and correct for Remi specifically. 'If at first you don't succeed, try, try again' is the conventional wisdom. Remi's version is 'if you don't first succeed, ram at full speed,' which removes the implied pause-and-reassess between the first failure and the second attempt and replaces it with escalating commitment. The second attempt should be faster and more committed than the first, not more considered.

This is not good engineering. It is very good Remi.

She hit her head against the bookshelf.

Waluigi is documenting the head impact not because it is surprising — Remi committed to a ram attempt and made contact with the obstacle at speed, the head impact is the predictable outcome of this approach — but because it is the most physically honest moment in the session. Everything else Remi did today was precise: the kneecap shot, the shadow blade cuts, the no to Mystic Morel, the table-sitting defiance. The bookshelf head impact is the exception. ## Pierce Anamatar:


The Candy, the Oracle, the Daggers, and the Contract

Waluigi needs to document Pierce Anamatar with appropriate care, because Pierce Anamatar is an entity the archive has not yet given full treatment to and the events of the 14th significantly expand the record.

Remi explained the full story.

Waluigi's sources do not provide the full text of Remi's explanation, but given the compressed nature of Remi's narrative style — and given that she is standing on a roof having just hit her head against a bookshelf and escaped through a window — Waluigi suspects the explanation included: the Shadow Estate, the portal artifacts, the need to go home, and the Oracle as an obstacle to all of the above.

Pierce Anamatar's first response was about the candy.

What, he said. Why would you accept candy from him. That makes you unable to attack him.

He was friendly, Remi said. Can you say no to candy.

Waluigi wants to document this exchange as the single most accurate summary of Remi's operating vulnerability available in the entire archive. It is more compressed than the birthday party. More compressed than the invisible ring. More compressed than the friendship contract or the guard with flowers. Can you say no to candy?

From the inside, accepting candy from someone friendly is not a failure of judgment. It is the completion of a social script. Someone offers something. You accept. The acceptance means you thought well of them. Remi thought well of the Oracle. The Oracle was friendly. The candy was friendly. The idea that friendly candy from a friendly person is a trap requires the receiver to be perpetually suspicious of all offers, which is a different way of moving through the world than Remi has ever chosen to adopt.

Pierce Anamatar apparently did not find this reasoning satisfactory.

So what should we do, Remi asked.

Fine, said Pierce Anamatar.

Waluigi wants to document the speed of this decision — fine — because it represents Pierce Anamatar arriving at a conclusion faster than most people would. The party has explained that they need to go home, that the Oracle is an obstacle, that the candy has created a complication. Pierce Anamatar said fine. Not: let me think about this. Not: what are you offering. Fine. The decision preceded the negotiation.

Then came the assessment of the prior attempt.

The green one already failed to kill him, Pierce Anamatar said.

YOU are incapable, he said. And your friend won't listen.

I'll do it.

Waluigi wants to document the specific content of Pierce Anamatar's capability assessment because it contains an implicit hierarchy: Green T attempted and failed, which makes Green T categorically incapable by Pierce Anamatar's framework. Remi is also categorically incapable, for reasons that may include the candy incident or may be broader. The friend who won't listen — Waluigi assumes Markop — is inaccessible through persuasion. Pierce Anamatar is therefore the only remaining viable option, which means Pierce Anamatar's willingness to do it is the deciding variable, and Pierce Anamatar has decided.

The 'I'll do it' is not an offer. It is a statement of what will happen.

Oh, okay, Remi said.

We're on a mission to go back home, she said.

Hmm, said Pierce Anamatar.

All we need now is a glass mirror.

Well, is that my problem.

It is A problem.

Well, look. If you kill the Oracle, this place will collapse and you will be spat out.

It sounds painful.

Yes. Very. To the Oracle. Not you.

Waluigi wants to document this as Disaster Inc.'s most efficient diplomatic outcome in the entire Shadow Estate arc. Remi negotiated, on a rooftop, after hitting her head against a bookshelf, while still needing to locate two portal artifacts, without any formal preparation, and arrived at: Pierce Anamatar kills the Oracle, the estate collapses, the party is expelled home. The mechanism for the party's exit is now contracted out to an external party whose capability Pierce Anamatar himself vouched for by identifying Green T's failure as evidence of incapability. Pierce Anamatar is not incapable.

Pierce Anamatar will do it.

The cost: a weapon.

Give me a weapon, Pierce Anamatar said.

Remi offered him a dagger. And one for a fallen comrade.

Not my comrade, Pierce Anamatar said. Someone else.

Waluigi needs to document the second dagger.

Remi carries a dagger that belonged to someone she does not know. She found it one day. She needed a weapon. She took it. The original owner was, apparently, someone who had fallen — someone who was no longer in a position to require the weapon — and Remi, who was in a position to require a weapon, took it.

This is the same logic she applied at age twelve crossing the Agora of Memes: available resource, current need, acquisition. The dagger is not Remi's by provenance. It is Remi's because she found it, needed it, and nobody else was there to use it.

Pierce Anamatar said the fallen comrade was vague. Remi agreed. She gave him a regular dagger.

He left.

Wait here, he said. Or not.

Waluigi finds 'or not' the most honest possible permission structure from an assassin who has just been contracted to collapse a dimension: he will do the job regardless of whether the party waits or moves. Their positional choices are irrelevant to his operational timeline. The 'or not' is not indifference. It is precision. He knows what he is going to do and they can organize themselves however they like around it.

## The Archivist's Head, the Scorncrow Defense, and the Guards Who Know Scorncrows Don't Bleed


Waluigi needs to step back in time to document what was happening in the other half of the estate while Remi was negotiating with Pierce Anamatar and finding the mundane mirror, because the parallel sequence is its own disaster and deserves full treatment.

Markop asked the skeleton — Rattles — how to open the bookcase.

Well, Rattles said. This really is rattling my funny bone. Maybe if you grew a spine you'd be able to force it open.

Waluigi wants to document that Rattles made two skeleton-specific puns within a single sentence of practical advice. Rattles has been with the party for a matter of hours and has already integrated skeleton wordplay into its operational communication style. Waluigi finds this concerning from an efficiency standpoint and admirable from a morale standpoint. The toads have their anthem. Rattles has puns. The Shadow Estate's servant corridors are hosting a comedy infrastructure.

Then the guards entered.

They were holding the Archivist's head.

Waluigi wants to document the specific horror of this — the Archivist's severed head, in the guards' hands, being used as evidence of a crime — because it is easy to read past it quickly in the momentum of the chase and Waluigi does not want it read past quickly. Vostolas the Archivist was executed by Remi approximately as recently as the prior session entry. He has been dead for a short time. And now his head is being carried through the corridors of the Shadow Estate as an accusatory exhibit.

Who did this, the guards asked.

Why is there blood on your axe.

Markop tried to explain. It was the scorncrow.

Scorcrows don't bleed, the guards said.

Waluigi needs to acknowledge that this is correct. Scorncrows do not bleed. Scorncrows are construct-adjacent entities — the estate's scarecrow guardian that the party has documented and declined to fight across multiple sessions. Constructs do not produce blood in any quantity that would explain an axe-coating. Markop's scorncrow defense was the least viable possible defense available given the physical evidence, and it failed immediately on its primary factual premise.

Don't devils disappear after death, Markop tried.

Why do we have his head then, the guards said.

They have a point. Devils, when they die in the material plane, typically disintegrate back to their home plane. Vostolas did not disintegrate. Vostolas remained sufficiently intact that his head is now a portable accusatory exhibit. This is either because the Shadow Estate's dimensional properties have altered the normal rules of devil death and dispersal, or because Vostolas was not a devil in the traditional sense, or because Remi's shadow blade did something that prevented the normal dispersal mechanism from activating.

Waluigi does not have a clean answer. What Waluigi has is: Vostolas's head is in a guard's hands, Markop's axe has blood on it, and the scorncrow defense failed.

Markop motioned for Rattles and Eager to run.

He pushed Salam out and ran.

The chase began.

## The Chase, Green T's Door, and the Ghosts Controlling Ghosts


Down a hallway, away from everyone, they saw a door open. Green T waved them down.

Waluigi wants to document Green T's timing a second time in this session entry because it has occurred twice now and the pattern is consistent: Green T is not present when the crisis begins, but Green T is present at precisely the moment when an exit is needed. Pierce Anamatar was contracted on the roof. The mundane mirror was found on the roof. Green T opened the door at the bottom of the stairs at the exact moment Markop and Rattles and Eager needed it opened.

Where Green T was during the guard chase. What Green T was doing that positioned him to open the correct door at the correct moment. These are questions Waluigi cannot answer from available sources. What Waluigi can document is that Green T's positional choices consistently place him at operational chokepoints precisely when the party needs them covered.

They ran through the door and out the window.

They ran more. They found a room with ghosts.

Waluigi's sources describe: ghosts controlling other ghosts, the controllers appearing to lead from the back.

Waluigi is filing this as significant intelligence about the Shadow Estate's supernatural population structure. The ghosts in the estate are not a uniform phenomenon. There is a hierarchy. Some ghosts are being controlled by others. The controllers operate from behind, which is the specific positional preference of entities that manage systems rather than engage directly — administrators, coordinators, the architectural layer beneath the visible one.

The estate has ghost middle management. Waluigi wants to know who the ghost executives are.

The party continued without engaging. Through a window, into the chess room.

## The Chess Room, the Losing White Pieces, and Eager's Shoes


A warmly lit and unusually comforting space, smelling pleasantly of incense and old books. Three plush armchairs around a low table with an ongoing chess match. White are losing quite badly. Behind an elegantly carved wooden screen, a large bed positioned to offer a view from every angle of the grand bay windows. Bookshelves along the south wall with provocatively and intriguingly titled spines.

Waluigi wants to note that this room is described as unusually comforting, which, combined with the serenity of the hidden hall, means the 14th of Harvestside has produced two rooms in the Shadow Estate with genuine positive atmospheric qualities. Both rooms are notable in the context of an estate that has otherwise specialized in threat, conspiracy, and servant corridors echoing with unsanctioned toad anthems.

The chess match. White losing quite badly. Waluigi is going to resist the temptation to read the chess position as allegory for the party's situation — Waluigi is not that kind of historian — but is going to note that an ongoing chess match in an empty room, with white losing quite badly, implies the match was interrupted at a specific moment by whoever was playing it, and that white was losing at the moment of interruption. Someone left this room while losing a chess game. They did not return to finish it. The game is still there. The losing position is preserved.

Markop checked a desk. A collection of teas — the blends seeming similar to the ones recovered from Vostolas.

Waluigi wants to document this connection because it is the second time the archive has recorded similar tea collections in separate rooms of the estate. Vostolas carried drugged bergamot tea. This desk contains teas that Markop identified as similar. The estate has a shared tea supply, or the estate has multiple operatives with access to the same prepared tea blends, or there is a tea-adjacent conspiracy operating across the estate's upper floors that Waluigi has not yet fully mapped.

Waluigi hopes the party's teas are clearly labeled.

Eager found a new pair of shoes. He put them on. He said: it feels wrong, wearing a dead person's shoes.

Well, Eager said. Pants are important.

Waluigi finds this reasonable on exactly zero grounds and is documenting it anyway because it is honest and because Eager's moral honesty is one of the things Waluigi values about him.

The pants were documented last session. The shoes are documented here. Eager's clothing situation continues to be resolved through the estate's deceased population.

## Ylana's Fountain


The east servant hall. Sparse and utilitarian. Wood floors. Doors along almost every wall. Echoing steps. Modest servant quarters behind every door.

Just outside a lavatory in the east end: an unframed painting on canvas stretched over wood. Flush against the wall. Red flowers in a vase, set outside against a stone backdrop. Overcast and grey. Something like a memorial site. A tiny inked label at the bottom corner, only just noticeable: Ylana's Fountain.

Waluigi wants to document Ylana's Fountain with the attention it deserves, because it is the third space on the 14th of Harvestside that has produced something with genuine feeling in it — the hidden hall's pastoral serenity, the chess room's incense and interrupted game, and now this. A painting in a servant corridor, unframed, flush against the wall outside a lavatory, labeled with a name and a word.

Ylana. The fountain. Red flowers against stone in an overcast grey. Memorial-site composition.

The placement matters. This is not a displayed painting. It is not in a gallery or a main corridor. It is in the east servant hall, outside a lavatory, flush against the wall in the most utilitarian part of the estate's upper floor. Someone put it there. Someone painted it, or brought it, and placed it in a location where it would be seen by people who used that corridor — which is to say, servants. People whose lives do not permit accumulation. People who move through the estate's utilitarian spaces.

Ylana. Waluigi does not have a prior record of this name in the Shadow Estate documentation. The fountain — a specific fountain, named, painted with flowers. A memorial. Someone died near a fountain. Someone painted it and put it where the servants would see it.

Waluigi is filing Ylana as a person who existed in the estate's history, whose death was significant enough that someone created this memorial and placed it in the servant corridor rather than a formal memorial space, which implies either that Ylana was herself a servant — placed in the space that belonged to people like her — or that whoever placed the painting wanted it to be in a place that would not be removed or questioned by the estate's main occupants.

The name is in the record. Waluigi will watch for it.

## The Doors, the Ghosts, the Anchor, and the Chest


Remi proceeded to open multiple doors.

This is Remi's characteristic approach to unexplored corridors — systematic, sequential, continuous. She does not stop to assess risk before each door because the assessment would slow the pace of discovery and Remi's operating principle in unexplored spaces is momentum. Each door is a door until it is something else. She opens them until something else happens.

Something else happened.

One door shut on her. She was ambushed by ghosts. The door was locked with an arcane lock. The ghosts surrounded her.

Waluigi wants to document Remi's decision-making in this moment as carefully as the kneecap shot and the execution, because it is the same category of decision even though it does not look like it.

She thought about running. Then she did not run. She chose to fight.

The phrasing in Waluigi's sources is specific: she chose. Not 'she fought because running was impossible.' Not 'the geometry of the room prevented escape.' She thought about running — the option existed, or she believed it existed — and she chose not to take it. She chose to fight.

She swung an anchor. It slammed into the ghost and dispersed it. The threat was disrupted. The door opened. The arcane lock was done.

Waluigi wants to document that Remi used an anchor. This is not a standard weapon. This is not the crossbow or the shadow blade or the dagger she carries. This is an anchor. A heavy, chain-attached object used for maritime purposes, present in the Shadow Estate for reasons the archive has not documented. Remi had access to it. She used it as a weapon against a ghost. It worked.

The anchor is the bookend to 'shiver me timbers' at the start of the session. The day began with a skeleton using nautical idiom. The day continues with Remi using nautical equipment as a ghost-dispersal tool. The Shadow Estate's servant corridors apparently have maritime influence that Waluigi has not yet fully explained.

Remi chose to fight. She won. The door opened.

Wario ran in.

He spotted a treasure chest.

He smashed it open.

Gold in his eyes, the chest broke open, loot everywhere.

Waluigi wants to end this session entry on Wario smashing the chest with his body in gold-fever, because it is the correct ending. The 14th of Harvestside has contained: a kneecap shot, a shadow blade execution, a head impact against a bookshelf, a purple toad warning, a hidden hall, an Oracle sighting, a rooftop negotiation, an assassination contract, a mundane mirror and five gold, a guard chase, a severed head, a scorncrow defense, the chess room, a lasso, an axe-wielding sheep thanking Green T, fifteen gold for Remi's return, missing supplies, Ylana's fountain, a ghost fight with an anchor, and Wario destroying a chest with his body.

All of this is the same day.

The chest is open. The loot is everywhere. Wario's eyes contain gold.

Two portal artifacts remain: the Mirror of True Reflection and the Umbral Signet.

Pierce Anamatar has a dagger and a contract.

Archie's supplies are gone.

Markop has a warning about himself that he has not been told.

The real Toadburt still has no one left to answer for him.

Ylana's fountain is painted in red flowers on grey stone in a corridor where only servants walk.

WAH.

name: The Spotlight Chase and the Cookie Siege
title: How Remi Was Lit Up by a Mocking Spotlight, Markop Promoted a Window into an Exit, Lyranth Accused the Wrong Toad of Crystal Possession, and the Party Hid in Tymnas’s Cottage Until Cookies Became a Security Incident
location: Shadow Estate corridors, trophy room, exterior grounds, and Tymnas’s cottage
type: Escape Sequence / Pursuit / Cottage Siege / Social Absurdity
status: Concluded — party temporarily hidden; Black Crystal still with Markop; enemy intelligence partially wrong
summary: After fleeing through the Shadow Estate, Remi was caught in a mocking spotlight as an Iron Dominion voice taunted the “Reborn” crew in song. Markop broke a stuck window with the Trowel of Retrieving, the party stumbled into a hellhound fight with Rattles, Eager panicked, Remi missed badly, Dan clumsily drove the beast off, and Lyranth appeared with knights demanding the Black Crystal from Eager — who did not have it. The group escaped through the trophy room, found Salam outside a window, and hid in Tymnas’s cottage, where Tymnas left for supplies, the Toads failed a bark-gathering errand, Eager learned nothing from a Tea Leaf Syndicate book, knights delivered suspicious cookies, Remi bit a raisin cookie, and the night ended in a pillow fort with Salam asleep on guard.
description:
Waluigi is documenting this sequence because it is a perfect example of how Disaster Inc. and its attached Toad constellation convert a simple retreat into a theatrical chase, a tactical error, a breakfast-table siege, an accidental tea criticism, a cookie incident, and a sleep arrangement that would make any military officer resign.

The party had already endured too much Shadow Estate nonsense for one night. Waluigi says this as a historian, which means the phrase "too much" is not emotional exaggeration but a professional measurement. They were running. Running was not a plan, but it was at least directionally honest. Sometimes survival begins as strategy and immediately degenerates into legs.

Then the spotlight found Remi.

This chase follows directly from the previous Shadow Estate chain. The party had survived the birthday trap, tangled with Vostolas, recruited Rattles, entered Tymnas's orbit, and acquired the Black Crystal through the servant-corridor artifact hunt. The estate is not chasing them because it enjoys cardio. It is chasing them because the group has become a moving breach in the manor's control system. The Black Crystal is an exit key, a ritual piece, and proof that the house can lose things.

The enemy's intelligence is therefore close but wrong. They know the crystal matters. They know the party has it. They do not know Markop is the carrier. That mistake turns this event from a simple pursuit into a useful diagnostic of enemy knowledge. Waluigi loves when enemies reveal the shape of their ignorance.

## The Spotlight


The spotlight is the moment the chase becomes ideological. Until that instant, the party is merely fleeing. Once the light hits Remi, the enemy is no longer only trying to catch bodies; it is trying to control the story of those bodies. This is the Shadow Estate's preferred method. It does not simply lock doors. It assigns roles. It does not simply send knights. It sends knights with a rhyme scheme.

Waluigi has seen this pattern before in aristocratic cruelty. The powerful enjoy making their victims participate in the scene of their own humiliation. A vote over dinner. A birthday party with a trapdoor. A spotlight in a corridor. These are not separate aesthetics. They are the same political habit wearing different costumes. The house wants the party to understand that even their panic has been staged.

A hard beam of light snapped onto Remi in the corridor, cutting through the gloom with the cruelty of a stage manager who had decided the child was now the protagonist of someone else's humiliation. The rest of the hallway remained dark enough to hide fear, but Remi was illuminated with theatrical precision. Waluigi hates theatrical precision when Waluigi is not the one using it.

A voice rang out, sing-song and mocking:

> Step into the spotlight, you pitiful crew!  
> The Iron Dominion is looking at you!  
> You call yourselves "Reborn," oh, isn't that grand?  
> The clumsiest comedy troupe in the land!  
> You're marching on castles, you're looking for fights,  
> But you can't even handle a handful of knights!  
> We set up a snare, and you walked right inside,  
> So swallow your ego and swallow your pride!

Waluigi has several objections. First, "Iron Dominion" is either a formal name, propaganda affectation, or someone in armor trying to sound larger than the squad actually present. Second, the meter is inconsistent. Third, mocking a fleeing group in song is powerful psychological warfare only when the target group has no Toads. This party had Toads.

Remi immediately objected that only Toads could sing.

This is not true in the biological sense, but it is true in the moral sense. Waluigi accepts the correction.

The Toads stared. Nobody knew whether they were offended by the enemy singing, by Remi's claim of Toad-exclusive performance rights, or by the fact that the enemy had chosen a format in which Toads would normally expect to dominate. Waluigi suspects all three.

## The Window That Would Not Open


Remi ran to a window and tried desperately to open it. This was a good instinct. Windows are doors for people with insufficient time and enough willingness to get scratched. Unfortunately, the window refused to cooperate. The Shadow Estate is a house with strong opinions about exits, and most of those opinions are hostile.

Remi pulled, shoved, rattled, and generally made the universal sound of a person discovering that architecture has chosen violence.

It did not open.

The Toads continued staring.

Markop then solved the problem with a trowel.

Specifically, Markop took his Trowel of Retrieving and smashed the glass. Waluigi appreciates this. Too many people treat magic items like delicate relics. Markop understands that a tool which retrieves can also remove the barrier between oneself and retrieval. The window broke. The escape route existed. This is why Waluigi respects practical people: they do not ask whether the window wants to be a door. They promote it.

The party ran.

## The Wrong Door, the Hellhound, and Rattles


The group fled through the broken window route and into another stretch of the estate. Remi opened another door with the bright doomed curiosity that has become one of her signature battlefield behaviors.

"Oh hey," she said, or something close enough in spirit. "I wonder what's in here."

Waluigi wants to state for the historical record that this sentence should be carved above the entrance to every haunted manor in every plane. It is the motto of people who survive impossible things and the reason they keep needing to.

The first door produced trouble. Hellhounds were involved. Rattles, who remains one of the most unexpectedly useful skeletons in Waluigi's current archive, engaged one of the beasts. The party had a moment to decide whether this was a run-past problem or a help-the-skeleton problem.

They chose to help Rattles.

This is morally good and tactically expensive, which is how one recognizes most Disaster Inc. decisions.

Markop formed the plan. He would come from one end. Eager would come from the other. The hellhound would be struck quickly, pinned between coordinated pressure, and dropped before the pursuit caught up. It was simple. It was sound. It required Eager not to panic.

Eager panicked.

Instead of closing and striking from the other side, Eager got scared, threw a simple dagger, and missed. The dagger clinked onto the floor with the sad little sound of a plan losing its second leg.

Waluigi is not judging Eager too harshly. Hellhounds are very convincing arguments against bravery. But the record must show the difference between the plan and the thing that happened where the plan used to be.

## The Empty Room and the Missed Arrows


While Markop and Rattles were now effectively alone with the hellhound, Remi ran to another door.

"Oh hey," the spirit of the moment repeated. "I wonder what's in here."

She opened it.

It was empty.

This is almost suspicious. In the Shadow Estate, an empty room is rarely empty because nothing is there. It is empty because the house is waiting for the emptiness to become useful later.

Markop called Remi back. They were fighting something over here, which is a sentence one should not have to say during a hellhound encounter but somehow did.

Remi responded by firing two arrows.

Both missed by a long shot.

Waluigi will not mock her too much. She had been spotlighted, chased, trapped, threatened, and forced through a broken window while the house continued inventing rooms. Accuracy suffers under these conditions. Still, the arrows missed so thoroughly that the target may have felt socially excluded.

Dan, meanwhile, decided to tend to Eager's injuries. This left Markop and Rattles handling the actual hellhound problem with insufficient help. Markop yelled for Dan to get over there.

Dan clumsily walked over and swung.

The hellhound screamed.

This is the part where incompetence briefly wrapped itself around success. Dan's swing connected with enough force or surprise to send the hellhound fleeing into another room. Waluigi has seen elegant swordplay. This was not that. But the hellhound did not care whether the technique was elegant. It cared that something had hit it and that continuing the discussion no longer seemed profitable.

## Knights, Lyranth, and the Black Crystal Mistake


This is where the event becomes strategically valuable. Everything before this is survival under pressure. Lyranth's accusation turns pressure into information. The enemy is not searching blindly. They have a target object and a target name. They are wrong about the name. Waluigi cannot overstate how useful that is. Bad intelligence is dangerous, but it is also a map of what the enemy thinks happened.

The Black Crystal's chain goes backward through the servant corridors, Vostolas's death, Rattles's recruitment, Mystic Morel's refusal to join, Green T's unrecorded choices, and the unresolved Toadburt question. It is a physical object carrying several prior scenes inside it. Lyranth demanding it from Eager means the estate's information network saw the object moving through the party but lost the exact handoff. Somewhere, someone stopped watching at the wrong second. Waluigi would like to thank that failure personally.

No sooner had the hellhound fled than knights appeared.

Because of course they did.

The Shadow Estate does not allow one problem to conclude without sending another to stand in the doorway holding paperwork for the next disaster. Knights moved in from multiple directions. Their timing suggested coordination. Their confidence suggested they believed the party had already been cornered. Their mistake was assuming the party knew what was happening.

Then Lyranth the Sculptor appeared at another door.

Waluigi pauses here because Lyranth is not just another pursuer. Lyranth is the medusa whose artistry converts living people into permanent décor. Her presence changed the temperature of the room. A knight can kill you. Lyranth can make your last expression part of someone else's collection.

She addressed Eager.

"Well, well, well. We know you have it, Eager. Hand over the Black Crystal. Our intelligence says you have it."

This was wrong.

Markop had the Black Crystal.

This mistake matters. Intelligence errors reveal the shape of the enemy's information network. The pursuers knew the Black Crystal was in the party's orbit. They knew it mattered. They believed Eager had it. That means they were tracking the object but not the handoff, or they were operating from old information, or someone deliberately fed them the wrong carrier. Waluigi does not yet know which. Waluigi knows only that the enemy was confident and wrong, which is one of Waluigi's favorite enemy conditions.

Eager, naturally, asked what the Black Crystal was and why it was important.

Lyranth did not appreciate the question.

"No jokes. Arrest him now."

The knights stormed the room from all sides, including through the old broken window route. Waluigi respects the use of the party's own escape damage as an enemy entry point. Waluigi hates it when done to Waluigi's allies, but Waluigi respects it.

## The Trophy Room


The trophy room is not just a room with exits. It is the estate explaining itself in taxidermy. The heads on the wall say: what enters this house can be classified, killed, preserved, and displayed. That message lands differently when Lyranth is behind you. The trophy room and the medusa are variations on the same idea: life made still for someone else's satisfaction.

This is why Remi remembering she left things in her room matters. In a normal house, going back for belongings is sentimental or practical. In the Shadow Estate, belongings become proof that a person still imagines a future where inventory matters. Markop's refusal is not coldness; it is triage. He understands that if they keep chasing every lost object, the house will eventually add them to the walls.

The party fled into a trophy room.

The room was a dim lounge, comfortably appointed and quiet in the way expensive rooms are quiet when they have been built to make death feel tasteful. Its walls carried a macabre gallery of furs and heads from exotic creatures. At first glance they resembled terrestrial beasts. At second glance they became wrong: the angles slightly off, the proportions not quite natural, the preserved faces suggesting ecosystems that should not be in the same house as a tea table.

Weapon racks lined the walls in several places, holding old weapons that were well made but otherwise unremarkable. Waluigi notes this because unremarkable old weapons in a haunted noble house are rarely unimportant. They may not be enchanted. They may not glow. But they are in a room designed to remember killing, which gives them context even if it does not give them magic.

Most importantly, the trophy room had five windows.

Five windows is not a decorative fact. Five windows means options. Five windows means angles of approach, possible escape routes, enemy entry points, line of sight, and at least five chances for the house to betray you with glass.

Remi said she had left stuff in her room.

Markop said they had everything they needed and that they should rest in the room.

This is a deeply Markop sentence. It is practical, exhausted, and correct enough to be annoying. When a building is trying to kill you, one must eventually stop chasing perfect inventory conditions and start asking where the next safe breath is located.

Then Markop opened a window and saw something poking out.

"What the hell is that thing?" he asked.

The thing was Salam.

Salam had somehow ended up outside the window.

Waluigi has stopped asking how Toads arrive in places. They are like mushrooms after rain: one turns around and there they are, somehow essential, possibly confused, and carrying a new problem.

They walked up to him. Salam was alive. This was good. It also meant the group was still not done moving.

"Alright," the spirit of the party said. "Let's go."

Markop wondered where Green T was.

Dan said to worry about it later because the knights were coming.

Dan was correct. Waluigi hates when panic produces accurate prioritization, but it does happen.

## Tymnas's House


Tymnas's cottage is not just a hiding place. Waluigi has said this before and will keep saying it until the reader stops treating warm rooms in death dimensions as cozy background. The cottage resists the Shadowfell's bleaching. It has food. It has books. It has the feeling of a life continuing beside a manor that converts life into etiquette and threat. That makes it a refuge. It also makes it a contradiction.

Contradictions attract plot. The party entering the cottage does not remove them from the estate's politics; it moves them into a quieter layer of those politics. Tymnas can leave for supplies. Others can know where he is. Cookies can arrive. A note can call him best friend. The cottage is therefore not outside the system. It is a pocket inside the system where the rules are softer, which may be more dangerous because softer rules invite tired people to breathe.

The group hid in Tymnas's cottage.

Tymnas was reading a book called *Fungi and You*.

Waluigi has not read *Fungi and You*, but the title alone suggests either a helpful gardening manual or a slow psychological trap. In the Shadow Estate, both options remain open.

Markop went to sleep. This was sensible. Markop had been carrying the party through physical danger, tactical decisions, and repeated architectural betrayal. Even centaurs with divine resilience require rest, and Waluigi refuses to judge anyone for sleeping after smashing windows, fighting hellhounds, and being chased by knights and a medusa.

Some time later, Tymnas left to get supplies from the manor.

The Toads left behind him.

Remi told them to take it easy and not get into trouble because she would be inside and they would be outside.

The Toads said they only needed some bark.

Bark, Waluigi notes, is never only bark when Toads are involved in a haunted cottage under pursuit conditions. Bark becomes woodcarving, decoy craft, snack theory, or the first step in a plan nobody fully admits is a plan.

"Don't worry," the Toads said in essence. "We got Dan. We'll be safe."

This sentence contains two errors. First, having Dan does not guarantee safety. Second, saying "we'll be safe" in the Shadow Estate is an invitation for the universe to clear its throat.

The Toads left to chop trees.

Then they remembered the woodcarving tool was broken. The situation outside was too hot. They went back inside.

Waluigi appreciates this rare display of risk assessment. The Toads evaluated the mission, identified a tool failure, considered the tactical temperature, and abandoned the errand. This is exactly what professionals do, except professionals use fewer pillow forts.

## Eager Reads the Tea Book


Eager found a book on the table and read from it.

It was a tea book. More specifically, it was a text in the tone of the Tea Leaf Syndicate:

> Tea is civilization distilled. In a single cup, you hold the labor of farmers, the wisdom of blenders, the patience of steepers, and the refined palate of centuries. To drink tea carelessly is to insult all of them.

The book continued with remarks about travel, trade, occasional acquisition through channels polite society would frown upon, and the Syndicate apologizing only for bad tea. It quoted the First Blender:

> A perfect cup requires perfect leaves, perfect water, perfect timing, and perfect company. Achieve three of four, and you may call yourself competent.

Waluigi recognizes the voice. Refined, criminal, petty about standards. The Tea Leaf Syndicate did not merely sell tea. They converted tea into hierarchy. Waluigi respects anyone who can make hot leaf water sound like a military doctrine.

Eager closed the book having learned nothing.

This is unfair to the book but accurate to Eager's mood. He then tried increasing his speed through training. Waluigi is not certain what form this training took inside a cottage under pursuit conditions, but Waluigi imagines short bursts of anxious movement and the quiet scraping of furniture that did not deserve this.

## The Cookie Delivery


The cookies are funny because they should not be here. They are also frightening for the same reason. A sword at the door is honest. A cookie at the door asks the exhausted mind to become polite. This is a different kind of attack. The party has to decide whether kindness is bait, whether bait can still be eaten, and whether a cookie shaped like Tymnas's head is affectionate, threatening, or simply the work of people with no normal social boundaries left.

Waluigi believes the cookies show the estate's emotional ecosystem leaking into the chase. The knights may be enemies, but the note speaks in the language of missing someone. Either the manor has people who genuinely care about Tymnas, or it has people willing to imitate care for tactical advantage. Both possibilities make the situation harder. It is easier to fight a monster than a social obligation with chocolate chips.

There was knocking at the door.

Knights stood outside.

They had cookies.

Waluigi needs the reader to understand that the Shadow Estate's horror is not limited to blood, mirrors, vampires, and petrification. Sometimes horror arrives with baked goods and the tone of a friendly errand.

The knights announced that they had brought cookies. Special delivery for Remi Remington. Was she there?

Remi said no. She was somewhere else.

Three knights were present. One checked a window and knocked.

"Hey, you Toad, open up. We need Tymnas. We baked cookies."

Eager blocked the door. Salam sat scratching his stomach, bored. Another Toad, Dan, lay side-faced on the door. The sound they heard was not being fully processed by him; it took two and a half minutes to register in his brain.

This is one of those details Waluigi could not invent because Waluigi's imagination has more dignity than reality.

Remi told the knights they were not there, but to leave the cookies in case Tymnas came back.

The knights walked off.

The party then faced a problem more dangerous than the knights: whether to accept the cookies.

Dan went to get them while the others kept an eye on him. This was a reasonable compromise. If cookies are poisoned, cursed, enchanted, or otherwise weaponized, one should send the person most willing to smell them first. Dan smelled the cookies. They smelled nice and toasty.

Remi brightened.

"Oooh cookies. I wonder what kind they are."

They were classic chocolate chip cookies.

"Oh boy!" Remi said.

Eager checked for magic and discrepancies. This was good. Waluigi appreciates suspicion applied to dessert. One cookie was in the shape of Tymnas's head. It said "Get well soon," badly spelled. There was a note on the back:

> To Tymnas, our best friend,  
> We miss you so much. You being cooped up in that cottage, you're going crazy. Please, we don't know the group name, but we play games and do puzzles and have fun. Please come back to the house.  
> From O.T.

Remi considered the faction name. Local Misfits, perhaps.

Dan suggested Toad-Headed Heroes.

Remi wondered why they announced themselves.

Waluigi agrees. If one is attempting manipulation through cookies, signing the note with a suspicious acronym is either incompetence, bait, or a faction branding exercise. Waluigi has seen all three.

Then Remi ate a cookie.

Dan asked whether she was sure she wanted to bite into it.

"It's a cookie," Remi's entire worldview replied. "How bad could it be?"

She realized she had bitten the raisin one.

"Noooooooooooo."

Waluigi records this as a genuine tragedy. Not the largest tragedy in the Shadow Estate, but one of the cleanest. Raisins pretending to be chocolate chips are deception without artistry. Waluigi condemns them.

## Night in the Cottage


The sleeping arrangement is ridiculous and revealing. Markop in Tymnas's bed shows that the person carrying the heaviest tactical burden is finally allowed to become a body instead of a plan. Remi near the Toad pillow fort shows that the group has rebuilt a child's idea of safety out of whatever soft objects remained. Salam asleep on guard is a failure, but it is also evidence that the body has limits the character sheet does not respect.

Waluigi wants the reader to notice that the party survives here not by defeating the estate, but by creating a tiny temporary society inside it. Bed. Pillow fort. Cookies. Watch. Toads. Sleep. Suspicion. These are domestic things, and the Shadow Estate hates domestic things that do not obey its hierarchy. Every unapproved nap is a small rebellion. Every shared room that does not become a trap is a theft from the house's authority.

As the day came to a close, Remi slept. There was no milk. There were Toads.

These facts may seem unrelated, but the emotional structure of the room depends on them. Cookies without milk are incomplete. Toads without supervision are a hazard. Remi sleeping near both suggests either trust, exhaustion, or the collapse of all remaining standards.

Salam took guard.

Then Salam fell asleep.

All together, the Toads huddled on the floor in a pillow fort next to Remi.

Markop slept in Tymnas's bed.

This is the final image Waluigi wants the reader to hold: a cottage in the Shadow Estate, a place of color inside a death dimension, containing a sleeping centaur in the bed, a child exhausted beside a Toad pillow fort, a guard who fell asleep, cookies of suspicious origin, a tea book with criminal standards, and enemies somewhere outside still believing they know who has the Black Crystal.

They did not.

Markop had it.

## The Cookie Note Naming Dispute


The naming dispute also reveals how the party is perceived from the outside. To themselves, they are a disaster held together by habit, guilt, loyalty, and whoever currently has the important object. To enemies, they become Reborn. To cookie-senders, they are unnamed visitors attached to Tymnas's absence. To Wario, they are a receivable. To Archie, they are probably something with the word heroes in it. To Waluigi, they are Disaster Inc. because Waluigi believes in accuracy even when accuracy is rude.

A name is a handle. If the party does not choose one, other people will grab whatever handle is convenient and drag them through the story by it. That is why the cookie note is not harmless. It proves the manor's social world is already discussing them without stable terminology. Rumor without a name becomes flexible. Flexible rumor becomes dangerous.

Waluigi is adding a separate note on the naming confusion because names are never just names. The cookie message said the senders did not know the group name. This is already funny because the group itself does not consistently know the group name. Disaster Inc., Freeroamer Heroes, Freeloader Zeros, Reborn, whatever the Iron Dominion thinks it is singing at — the party's brand identity is less a banner and more a pile of contested napkins.

Remi guessed the cookie faction might be called **Local Misfits**. This is a strong guess in the sense that it sounds like a group of people who would bake Tymnas-head cookies and sign them with suspicious initials. Dan proposed **Toad-Headed Heroes**, which is less a faction name than a symptom, but Waluigi respects the confidence. The important detail is that everyone immediately began treating the unsigned social signal as a branding problem.

This matters because the Shadow Estate runs on names, titles, invitations, roles, and performances. If the party cannot stabilize its own name, enemies can assign one. The Iron Dominion calls them Reborn. The cookie note cannot name them. Wario would monetize three names at once. Archie would try to make one inspirational. Waluigi would choose the correct name and then be ignored until history vindicates him.

The cookie note therefore belongs in the same family of disputes as the larger Disaster Inc. naming crisis. It is smaller, stranger, and covered in crumbs, but it proves the same point: a group without a settled name is vulnerable to being narrated by its enemies. WAH.

## Waluigi's


Assessment

Read this event beside the birthday trap, the Rattles corridor, the gardener vote, and the naming dispute. It becomes clearer as a continuation of one long argument between the party and the Shadow Estate over who gets to define reality. The estate says guest, prisoner, bride, statue, performer, carrier, criminal. The party keeps answering with broken windows, wrong doors, skeleton allies, pillow forts, and names nobody agrees on.

That is why this event matters beyond the chase. It shows the estate losing narrative control even while retaining tactical danger. The enemy can light the stage, but Remi can heckle the premise. The enemy can demand the Black Crystal, but from the wrong person. The enemy can bring cookies, but cannot prevent the cookies from becoming a debate about group branding and raisins. Control remains powerful. It is no longer complete.

This event matters for several reasons.

First, the enemy's intelligence is close but flawed. They know the Black Crystal matters. They know it is with the party. They misidentify Eager as the carrier. This gives the party a narrow advantage if they realize it in time.

Second, Remi's behavior shows the strain of repeated pursuit. She remains curious, fast, and willing to act, but she is also making door choices under pressure and missing shots badly. Waluigi refuses to reduce this to incompetence. Stress bends skill.

Third, Markop continues to function as the party's practical center. He breaks windows, calls people back to fights, protects the objective, chooses rest over perfect inventory, and sleeps when sleep is tactically necessary. Waluigi approves.

Fourth, the Toads remain impossible. They can turn an escape sequence into a debate about singing rights, a tree-bark errand into a reversed decision, and a siege into a cookie protocol. Waluigi does not understand them. Waluigi respects them in the way one respects weather.

Fifth, Tymnas's cottage is becoming more than a hiding place. It is a social node. The knights' cookie note suggests others in the house miss him, need him, or are trying to lure him back. The cottage is not isolated from the manor's emotional ecosystem. That makes it useful and dangerous.

Finally, the event shows the Shadow Estate's most exhausting quality: it does not separate horror from comedy. A medusa demands a crystal. A hellhound flees from a clumsy blow. Knights arrive with cookies. A raisin ruins Remi's hope. Everyone sleeps in a cottage where the guard has fallen asleep.

This is not tonal inconsistency. This is the Shadow Estate. Terror and absurdity are roommates, and neither pays rent.

One more point: the cottage rest also marks a shift in scale. Earlier Shadow Estate scenes are about courts, artifacts, portals, and aristocratic murder games. This scene ends with people trying to sleep near cookies. That reduction is not a loss of importance. It is the point. Grand crises are survived in small rooms by tired people making bad security decisions with the materials available. Waluigi trusts histories that remember the pillow fort more than histories that only remember the crystal. The crystal matters because it may open a way out. The pillow fort matters because it proves there are still people worth getting out.


Waluigi also notes the absence of triumph. Nobody wins a medal for this night. Nobody claims a throne. Nobody solves the manor. They gain one more hour, one more room, one more chance to wake up and make a better mistake. In the Shadow Estate, that is not nothing. That is the campaign breathing through its teeth.


And yes, Waluigi counts that as progress, because progress in this house arrives wearing bruises and crumbs.


WAH WAH WAH.
